transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Time: 14:00 - 14:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Grace Lin (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood TAM), Priya Menon (AtlasPay), Mark Rivers (AtlasPay, procurement), Dana Cho (AtlasPay InfoSec), Ethan Lowe (AtlasPay SRE), Claire Bennett (AtlasPay legal)

Summary:
- Preflight between Redwood and AtlasPay focused on privileged key handling, KMS/escrow requirements, SLA escalation path, and pricing for dedicated vs private deployments.
- AtlasPay has strong constraints around key custody, egress, and SOC2 plus ISO requirements. They want clarity on KMS integrations and an approval path for privileged keying.
- Redwood to provide DPA redlines, SOC2 evidence, and run targeted latency + cold-start benches on Dedicated.

Topics:
- Privileged key custody (KMS/HSM, key escrow concerns)
- SLA tiers, escalation and rollback playbook
- Private deployment (VPC, on-prem) vs Dedicated capacity tradeoffs
- Pricing and procurement timeline
- Benchmark plan and pilot kickoff

Action items (captured during call):
- See action_items metadata field above for owners/due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Grace Lin: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. we wanted to run through the privileged key ask, sla escalation and make sure legal and infra have a path to approve. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Priya Menon: Priya here, head of platform at AtlasPay. we own infra and the integration.
[00:18] Mark Rivers: Mark, procurement, i'll be shepherding contract side.
[00:21] Dana Cho: Dana, i lead infosec; mainly here for KMS and any key custody questions.
[00:26] Ethan Lowe: Ethan, SRE. also looking at latencies and peering.
[00:30] Claire Bennett: Claire - legal counsel for AtlasPay.
[00:32] Miguel Alvarez: Hi team, Miguel from Redwood SE. i'll take the tech part.
[00:36] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, TAM. i'll coordinate the pilot steps.

[02:05] Grace Lin: Quick agenda: 1) KMS and escrow constraints 2) SLA tiers and who we call at 3) pricing for Dedicated/Private 4) bench plan. If anything missing shout.

[03:10] Dana Cho: The ask from compliance: AtlasPay has to control all high-privilege keys, no third-party key-holding in production without an approval exception. we do have limited exceptions for managed KMS where keys are in our cloud vendor KMS but not in a vendor-managed HSM. curious how Redwood supports customer-managed keys and if there is any scenario where Redwood would need access.

[03:47] Miguel Alvarez: Right. so Redwood Private supports a customer-managed KMS via bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration; for Dedicated we can also configure a tenant-local KMS. We do have an optional key-escrow flow for hot migration/restore but that flow is gated behind legal sign-off and can be disabled.

[04:10] Dana Cho: When you say 'key-escrow' can you clarify who holds the key and under what circumstances Redwood would unwrap tokens? that's our big redline.

[04:25] Miguel Alvarez: Sure — apologies if i'm being wordy. The default is we never hold customer private keys. If you opt into the escrow service, the escrow is sealed in a multi-party HSM procedure: an HSM operator plus a Red-ops approval step; for AtlasPay we can map that to a restricted set of personnel, and we can require a quorum using your KMS roots. But if you don't want escrow at all we can run without it — just BYOK.

[05:02] Dana Cho: That sounds closer, but Claire will want to see the exact control matrix. Also we need to understand what logs are produced on key usage — audit logs.

[05:18] Miguel Alvarez: We emit KMS audit events and include key usage logs in the platform audit trail. There's a per-tenant audit bucket that can be forwarded to your SIEM; we also support signed PKCS logs for key unwrap events. note: might be transcribed as pkcs or pcs, apologies.

[06:00] Claire Bennett: From legal perspective, escrow is a high hurdle. we need a written runbook and a list of authorized roles. any access must be logged and auditable for our audits. is that covered?

[06:20] Sanjay Patel: Yes, we can provide runbooks and the access list as part of the onboarding packet. Redwood can also agree to notify AtlasPay prior to any key-escrow operation unless it's a critical incident — we can document SLA windows.

[07:05] Mark Rivers: On pricing — high level: we need a committed cost for Dedicated capacity (monthly) vs a Private deployment (one time + infra). we also need to understand egress and data-transfer fees, especially if we use a multi-region fallback.

[07:35] Grace Lin: Absolutely; we'll send a pricing spreadsheet after this call that lays out: hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved templates (monthly commitment tiers), and Private deployment estimates (license + infra ops). any particular skews we should call out?

[07:55] Mark Rivers: We care about p99 latency SLOs — if those aren't met, the SLA credits need clarity. also escalation chain in procurement.

[08:20] Miguel Alvarez: For p99 we publish numbers per model/instance type; for Dedicated we can commit to lower p99 with reserved capacity. SLA credit mechanics: typically credits are applied when a monthly uptime or latency threshold is missed and are pro-rated. We can document escalation steps and on-call contacts for Priority 1s.

[09:10] Dana Cho: What about fallback policies? if a Dedicated pool is overloaded can you route to hosted fallback and what are the data residency implications?

[09:30] Miguel Alvarez: We have smart routing. In general, we can route by policy — latency first or cost first. Fallback to hosted is possible but only if you opt in; we can restrict that to models that are equivalent and ensure logs and data residency meet your constraints. We can also restrict fallback to a same-region hosted cluster or to your Private deployment.

[10:04] Ethan Lowe: For our SREs, the top items are: cold-start behavior, warm KV cache performance, and multi-tenancy isolation. Miguel, can you speak to cold-start numbers so we get an idea of impact on tail latency?

[10:20] Miguel Alvarez: Sure — our recent p99 cold-start on rtx-something nic… sorry, the specific GPU name might be mangled in the transcript. But typical cold-start p99 for the sequence lengths you sent is ~350-450ms on Dedicated with warm cache it drops to ~30-60ms. We'll run a bench soon with your actual traffic shape.

[11:00] Priya Menon: That's promising. For compliance we also need retention windows for input/output data, and if Redwood retains any data for debugging.

[11:16] Grace Lin: Redwood retains minimal logs; customers can opt for no retention for inference payloads on Private. Hosted and Dedicated by default retain short-term request metadata for billing and debugging, retention windows are configurable and documented in the DPA. We'll include the default retention values in the DPA redline packet.

[12:05] Claire Bennett: On the DPA: we have specific language around sub-processing and data residency. would Redwood accept a clause that prevents any cross-border fallback unless explicitly approved by AtlasPay?

[12:25] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, we can put routing policies in the contract: route by region and disallow cross-border fallback unless authorized. That's a standard enterprise request.

[13:00] Mark Rivers: Another procurement point — we need an SLA escalation ladder: contact names/titles, response times for P1/P2, and an ability to request a rollback if a model rollout causes regressions.

[13:20] Sanjay Patel: We have a runbook: P1 — 15m ack, P1 triage within 1h, P2 — 1h ack, P2 triage within 4h. Rollbacks can be automated via traffic policy; we can schedule canary rollouts with auto-fallback. We'll share the runbook with Claire and Priya.

[14:10] Dana Cho: For key custody, is there any scenario where Redwood would ask AtlasPay to provide a key material to Redwood for onboarding? our policy is avoid exporting root keys.

[14:33] Miguel Alvarez: We don't require root key export. For BYOK we ask for a wrapped key package and the steps to integrate to your KMS; we support SAML-based ephemeral key exchange or a sealed wrapped key. If you prefer an on-site HSM we can accept an HSM-backed connection.

[15:00] Claire Bennett: Language-wise legal will redline the escrow and 'access on request' clauses. we'll want specifics on who can approve and timestamps in the audit logs.

[15:25] Grace Lin: Understood. we'll include a proposed clause and a control matrix showing roles that can approve escrow unwrapping.

[16:00] Ethan Lowe: Miguel can you talk about network layout — peering, VPC peering vs VPN, and whether you support transit gateway? we need to know if traffic will traverse public internet for certain flows.

[16:22] Miguel Alvarez: We support direct VPC peering in most cloud providers and can also establish private endpoints. Transit gateway support varies by region but typically yes. For Private deployments on-prem we can arrange a bastion/collector and a dedicated control plane in your VPC.

[17:05] Priya Menon: Are there any limitations on model size or sequence length for Dedicated that would affect our workload? we have a few long-context models in our evaluation set.

[17:26] Miguel Alvarez: We have model profiles; some of the longer contexts are best on Dedicated with higher-memory instance shapes. We'll map your model sizes to recommended instance types in the bench run results. Also quantization and kernel selection can shift the cost numbers; we'll show tradeoffs.

[18:10] Mark Rivers: For pricing, does Redwood include the KMS costs or is that separate? also any per-request surcharge for KMS unwraps?

[18:30] Grace Lin: KMS costs are typically billed to the customer (AtlasPay) since it's your cloud KMS. If you use Redwood-managed escrow HSM there may be an operational fee; we will call that out in the pricing spreadsheet.

[19:05] Claire Bennett: Let's talk timeline. procurement wants to close by mid-November if possible. what's realistic for a pilot and for legal sign-off?

[19:25] Grace Lin: If legal gets our DPA redlines by Friday, we can have a pilot kickoff the week after next. Pilot duration typically 2-4 weeks. Full Dedicated onboarding tends to take 4-6 weeks from pilot acceptance.

[20:02] Priya Menon: That aligns with our timeline. we need to validate security docs and run the bench before committing.

[21:00] Miguel Alvarez: For the bench plan: we'll need your traffic sample (1hr representative) and we'll run a bench with both warm and cold KV cache scenarios, multi-region failover test, and p99/P50 metrics. We'll share raw logs and a summarized sheet.

[22:10] Ethan Lowe: We'll provide a traffic profile and peering topology. also want to capture tokenization differences — do you have consistent tokenizer for the models we're testing?

[22:32] Miguel Alvarez: Tokenization is model-specific. If you share the model names we'll ensure the bench uses matching tokenizers and include token counts in the results. slight mis-transcription possible e.g., 'tokanizer' in the FR.

[23:15] Mark Rivers: On the commercial ask: what sort of commitment discounts do you offer for 12-month Dedicated vs 36-month?

[23:35] Grace Lin: Discounts increase with term and capacity. We'll include examples: 12-month 10% off list at certain tiers, 36-month up to 20% for larger commits. exact numbers in the spreadsheet.

[24:20] Claire Bennett: Any third parties involved in your infra chain we should flag in the DPA? subprocessors?

[24:40] Miguel Alvarez: We list subprocessors in the DPA appendices — typically cloud infra providers and CDN partners. We'll surface the current list and update you if any changes occur.

[25:10] Dana Cho: For encryption in transit, is mutual TLS supported between our VPC and Redwood endpoints?

[25:25] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints and we can do cert pinning on our side.

[26:00] Priya Menon: Are there limitations around audit log retention? we have a 7 year retention for certain audit trails for payments.

[26:18] Sanjay Patel: We can provide export of audit logs to your bucket with configurable retention; long-term archival (7 years) would be customer-managed in your storage. we retain high-frequency logs for shorter windows for performance.

[27:05] Ethan Lowe: A question on incident drills — would Redwood participate in a joint incident tabletop for our payment flow?

[27:20] Grace Lin: Absolutely. We can schedule a tabletop with our on-call and your SREs as part of pilot. We'll capture the drill outcomes and refine the runbook.

[28:10] Mark Rivers: Back to legal — Claire will push DPA redlines. can Redwood accept a short negotiation window to accelerate procurement?

[28:28] Claire Bennett: We'll try to consolidate comments to speed up. timeline depends on escrow acceptance.

[29:00] Miguel Alvarez: One more tech caveat — if you want absolute zero retention on inference payloads for hosted paths, we can discuss an anonymization flow but it affects our ability to debug. Private and Dedicated give you more control there.

[29:45] Priya Menon: Good to note. we prefer Dedicated for critical payment flows because of predictability and control.

[30:10] Grace Lin: Ok recap so far: 1) Redwood to send DPA redline summary + SOC2/ISO artifacts 2) Miguel to run a bench with AtlasPay traffic profile (warm/cold) 3) pricing spreadsheet for Dedicated vs Private 4) schedule pilot kickoff for week of 11/02 pending legal review.

[31:05] Claire Bennett: We'll review DPA and respond with a consolidated redline. specifically we'll highlight escrow and cross-border routing.

[31:40] Ethan Lowe: we'll prepare the traffic sample and peering info; i'll drop it in the shared drive.

[32:20] Sanjay Patel: i'll follow up with a proposed pilot schedule and the runbook template.

[33:10] Mark Rivers: For procurement path — if pilot looks good, we want a simple SOW and a template PO process. can Redwood accept a PO with a one-time private license if needed?

[33:35] Grace Lin: Yes we can accept a PO; for Private deployments there's usually a license + implementation fee, we can map that out.

[34:02] Dana Cho: slight thing — can we get a sample of your audit logs schema so our SIEM team can parse them?

[34:18] Miguel Alvarez: yes, we'll share the schema and a sample bundle.

[35:00] Priya Menon: Any concerns about vendor lock-in, we want an exit path?

[35:15] Miguel Alvarez: We support export of model artifacts and KV caches in standard formats. We can include an exit clause for data export in the DPA/SOW.

[36:02] Claire Bennett: We'll also need continuity of service language around key revocation and transfer.

[36:20] Grace Lin: Noted, we'll propose language.

[37:10] Mark Rivers: Are there any immediate red flags from Redwood's side about AtlasyPay's constraints?

[37:25] Miguel Alvarez: No red flags; it's mostly documentation and configuration. Escrow is the main legal lift but technically feasible. We'll need a little bit of engineering time to map the BYOK flows.

[38:05] Ethan Lowe: I'd like the bench results to include p50/p95/p99 and cold-start traces — that'll help us size capacity.

[38:35] Miguel Alvarez: Will do. We'll also include KV cache hit rates and cold-warm heatmaps.

[39:10] Priya Menon: On fallback, if we disallow cross-border fallback we need to understand capacity constraints in region — can Redwood provide surge capacity?

[39:33] Sanjay Patel: We have burst capacity options and reserved autoscaling. We can document burst behavior and warm pools for your traffic shape.

[40:05] Claire Bennett: Let's set a follow-up where legal and Redwood legal talk directly — can we do that next week?

[40:18] Grace Lin: Yes, we can schedule a legal-to-legal 30 minute sync. How's next Thursday 10am?

[40:25] Claire Bennett: Works for me.

[41:00] Mark Rivers: And AE to procurement touchpoint— i'll expect the pricing sheet.

[41:10] Grace Lin: I'll send it by Friday EOD.

[42:05] Miguel Alvarez: Minor note, we mentioned subprocessors earlier — i'll attach the current subprocessors list to the DPA packet.

[43:00] Priya Menon: Sounds like good progress. we'll aim for pilot kickoff once we review the bench results and redlines.

[44:12] Grace Lin: Recap of next steps aloud: 1) Grace sends DPA redline summary + SOC2 link by Fri; 2) Miguel runs bench and shares results by next Tue; 3) Pricing sheet for Dedicated/Private by Fri; 4) Legal-to-legal 30m next Thursday 10am; 5) AtlasPay to send traffic sample and peering info by Mon.

[45:00] Claire Bennett: Thanks all. we'll consolidate legal comments and aim to be quick about escrow gating.

[45:32] Mark Rivers: Appreciate the clear path.

[46:15] Grace Lin: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and send the links.

[46:40] Miguel Alvarez: Thanks, bye.

[47:00] (recording stopped)

Notes about transcript: occasional transcription errors on acronyms (KMS/KMZ, PKCS vs PCS) and GPU names. speakers sometimes overlap.
